findings.title: Reject ambiguous highest-priority crypto providers
findings.body: DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return order 200. When more than one is present, sorting leaves their relative order dependent on ServiceLoader discovery order and the first is silently selected. Previously this configuration failed explicitly. In particular, a classpath containing both the default and FIPS providers can now select the non-FIPS implementation instead of rejecting an ambiguous security configuration. Reject ties at the highest priority (while still allowing the lower-priority authz provider), or introduce an explicit selection mechanism.

findings.title: Exercise the actual curves and verify the converted signatures
findings.body: Every test generates the same default EC key, which is P-256 on the standard JDK provider. Selecting SHA384withECDSA or SHA512withECDSA does not change that key's curve, so the ES384 and ES512 tests merely pad P-256 signature components. Consequently, the ES512 test never exercises the long-form DER sequence length required by real P-521 signatures. The assertion also checks only the converter against itself, allowing a consistently incorrect conversion to pass. Generate keys explicitly using secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1, and verify the reconstructed DER signature with JCA (or compare it with the original DER signature).
